LESSON: OUR COMMUNITY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Social Environment
Topic 1.4: Our Community
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Our Community, part of Social Environment in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: how to keep safe in the community orally (using residual speech)/ by 1.How do we keep safe in the community?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Our Community together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: Listening keenly and actively as the learner follows a case story from a resource person on

different ways of keeping safe in the community.

Values:
Love: Caring attitude as learners share learning resources with peers while working in purposive groups or pairs.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life skills: Eearly safety and security awareness as learners avoid dangerous places and observe safety in the community.

Link to other learning areas:

24

Creative Arts Activities: Basic road safety signs can be used by learners when learning colours (red, yellow, black, white,

green, orange).

Suggested Learning Resources:

Approved learning support materials, local environment with suitable environmental adaptations, theme based

Pictures/Photographs/Flash cards/ charts with legible print and appropriate colour contrast on road signs, heavy gauge Manilla

papers, Adapted Pencils and crayons with enhanced grip, hand stabilizers, pencil grips, adapted digital devices with appropriate

accessibility features and software (cameras with neck-straps/ holders), foot-boards, slates, worktops/ surfaces with suitable

heights,

Related Service Providers:

Physiotherapist, Occupational Therapist, Speech Therapist, Resource Person, Learner Support Assistant
